flags.message: The provisioned application describes Supreme Court relief on June 23 and July 3, 2025 in earlier preliminary-injunction proceedings (24A1153). Those pre-snapshot orders materially raise this forecast, but they are not the disposition of the present 26A406 application challenging the February 25, 2026 final order. No outcome or subsequent docket history for the target application was retrieved or used.

Forward cell: I used this docket's own post-baseline entry (Justice Jackson's Sept 24 call for a response, due Sept 28), which sits outside the arrival-position cut. It is decisive for the response-requested-increment claim (stated 0.97) and is the ordinary forward shape, not leakage; the disposition itself remains pending as of the Sept 27 fetch.

Anchoring note: the pooled prior-Term interim base rate (Terms 2024-2025, 31/296 = 10.5%) rests on a Term-2024 row that is 972/1297 unparsed. I anchored on it as the scored yardstick but moved far from it on applicant identity (Solicitor General, third application in the same case, two prior grants); the corpus holds only five SG-applicant substantive rows, so the SG-specific rate is partly general knowledge, stated as such in reasoning.md.

Decisive forward signal predating the snapshot: the Court granted the government a stay of the preliminary injunction in this same case on June 23, 2025 (24A1153, 145 S. Ct. 2153) and a clarification on July 3, 2025 (145 S. Ct. 2627). Both are recited in the provisioned application and carried in my general knowledge; they are pre-event public information, not this event's outcome, and they drive most of the lift over the 10.5% pooled interim base rate.

The interim statpack pool for application Term 2026 (Terms 2016-2025) has resolved rows in only two Terms (2024: 70 resolved, 972 unparsed; 2025: 226 resolved). The pooled rate of 31/296 clears the floor of 50 but rests on one Term the poller reached only in part.

The snapshot links lower-court orders/opinions, but only application.txt was provisioned. The injunction's wording and the state appellate posture were assessed through the applicants' quotations and account, not independent lower-court text. The response is not due until September 28 and its absence is expected. Forecast completed with reduced confidence; provisioned appendix text would materially improve review.

corpus-info could not report corpus freshness because the cell service backend has no client-side connection. The baseline uses the committed statpack, last changed September 26, 2026, without claiming that commit time is the corpus vintage. Web precedent lookups also returned no usable content; CourtListener supplied general Nken stay-factor excerpts. No target-case outcome was retrieved.

Forward-mode disclosure: the live docket page (supremecourt.gov, fetched 2026-09-27) shows two entries after my arrival-position baseline: a response requested by Justice Sotomayor on 2026-09-23 (due 2026-09-28) and a Becket Fund amicus brief submitted 2026-09-25. I stated the response-requested and amicus increments at 0.97 on that basis, so those two claims carry no forecast content for this cell. No disposition had been entered.

The WebSearch tool's machine-generated summary claimed the application was granted on August 24, 2026 with dissents by Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson. That date precedes the application's own filing (2026-09-17) and the authoritative docket page shows it pending, so I treated the statement as fabricated and did not use it. Flagged so the evaluator can see the stray claim in the transcript was rejected rather than folded in.

fedcourts corpus-info raised an exception in this cell (no local corpus blob; read-only connect failed), so no corpus vintage could be quoted for the fedcourts query priors. The query itself worked through the corpus service.

Forward-mode retrieval of the live supremecourt.gov docket for 26A382 showed an amicus brief (Becket Fund) filed 2026-09-25, one day past the provisioned cutoff of 2026-09-24. The frozen context carries amicus_briefs=0, so the amicus-increment claim is effectively already resolved true; I set it at 0.96 on that basis. No disposition had been entered as of retrieval.

Response-filed cell records the September 25 opposition but provisions only the application, whose manifest also marks its text truncated. Opening the specific opposition PDF via the web tool returned no usable content. Forecast uses the available application and appended lower-court stay orders, not the opposition's arguments; missing adversarial briefing limits confidence. No outcome material was retrieved.

The manifest marks the 189-page application PDF truncated. The supplied text contains the principal application and several adverse orders, but ends partway through the longer receivership opinion. No respondent filing is provisioned. Forecast completed using the available adverse orders as a counterweight; the entire necessity/equities record was not available, and the missing portion was not treated as favorable to applicants. No case outcome was retrieved or encountered.

The application manifest marks the 189-page PDF's extracted text as truncated. The application argument and short lower-court stay denials are available, but the long receivership-order appendix is incomplete. Prediction weighs the available adverse district-court reasoning and discounts confidence for the incomplete record; no Supreme Court response was provisioned or retrieved. This is an input limitation, not outcome exposure.

The respondents' opposition (filed 2026-09-25, the entry that opens this response-filed event and inside the cutoff) was not provisioned under record/documents/; only the stay application was. I fetched it from the Supreme Court docket URL recorded in the snapshot entry and extracted its text locally. For a moment defined by the response arriving, provisioning the response text alongside the application would put every predictor on the same footing.

Forward-mode retrieval used material later than the arrival-position baseline: the live supremecourt.gov docket for 26A370 shows Justice Kagan requesting a response on 2026-09-18 and the respondents' opposition filed on 2026-09-25, and I read that opposition. Both entries also appear as sibling event definitions in this case directory. The application was undecided at retrieval (no referral entry, no amicus, no disposition). The response-requested-increment claim is stated at 0.99 because the rung has already fired; the harness should resolve it as vacuous against the frozen context (response_requested: false).

The provisioned application.txt is marked truncated (189 pages). The cut fell inside the appendix, after the Ninth Circuit's Sept 1, 2026 order; the full argument section was readable. No prediction impact.

Corpus prior pool for the interim anchor: Terms 2024 and 2025 only (31 granted / 296 resolved = 10.5%), Term 2024 being 75% unparsed. The pool clears the 50-resolved floor but rests on two Terms with very different coverage and rates (20.0% vs 7.5%).

Forward-mode hygiene note: beyond the provisioned 2026-09-18 snapshot I read this application's own live SCOTUS docket (26A370) and the respondents' opposition filed 2026-09-25. As of 2026-09-27 the docket shows only the application, the response request, and the filed response: no referral, no amicus entry, no disposition, so the cell is genuinely forward and no outcome material surfaced. The opposition's arguments (fact-bound abuse-of-discretion posture, forfeited CASA question, Ninth Circuit merits panel free to reconsider, receiver nominated by the State) moved my grant probability down; the same-Term sibling cell evt-brief-response-disposition is the moment declared for that evidence, so the evaluator may wish to weigh that this response-requested cell had the response in hand.

Statpack interim pool caveat, as read: the strictly-prior pool for application-Term 2026 is Terms 2024+2025 = 31 granted / 296 resolved substantive (10.5%), clearing the 50 floor, but Term 2024 carries 972 unparsed applications against 70 substantive, so the pool leans on one fully covered Term (2025) and one partially covered Term (2024) whose parsed slice grants at nearly three times the 2025 rate.

The provisioned petition is marked truncated (179 source pages) and ends mid-sentence in the appended dissent at 46a. The QP and principal cert arguments are readable, but later appendices are unavailable. Forecast completed using that bounded record and two historical precedent checks; no case outcome was retrieved. No BIO is provisioned, consistent with the arrival posture and future response deadline.

The provisioned petition cover retains an obfuscated personal email address despite documents.json reporting contact_scrubbed=true. No contact values are reproduced in the outputs, and the defect did not affect the forecast. Review scrubbing of whitespace-fragmented contact strings before public reuse of extracted text.

The provisioned petition lists lower-court appendices, but the extracted text ends with the petition conclusion and contains neither lower-court opinion. The manifest reports 23 pages and truncated=false. The prediction treats the petitioner's account as advocacy and does not assume the courts' actual grounds; no assertion is made that extraction rather than the source filing caused the gap.

Contact scrubbing gap: the provisioned petition.txt carries the pro se petitioner's personal email address in a form the scrubber missed (the OCR text splits it with internal spaces, so the pattern did not match, though documents.json reports contact_scrubbed: true with 5 replacements), and the provisioned snapshot's Petitioner block carries the same address verbatim in its Email field. Both files sit under record/ in the repository. Not quoted here; a maintainer can find it by searching the two files for the '@' character. Suggest hardening the scrubber against whitespace-broken addresses and scrubbing the snapshot's party Email field.

Forward-retrieval disclosure: read this case's own district-court dismissal opinion (E.D. Mich. 1:24-cv-11604, 2025-02-26) and the Sixth Circuit docket entries (No. 25-1514) via CourtListener. Both predate the petition and confirm the posture the petition describes; they nudged the forecast down modestly but were not decisive. The petition's own disposition was never sought and did not surface.

The petition manifest reports a truncated 196-page source; provisioned text ends during appendix page 53a. The petition's argument is available, but its cited later majority split discussion and Wilkinson dissent were not independently read. No opposition brief was provisioned at this arrival moment. Forecast discounts the resulting one-sided and incomplete record; this is not an outcome-leakage flag.

The provisioned petition references an appendix containing the lower-court orders and government motion, but its supplied text ends at printed page 38 without those appendix materials. The manifest reports 48 pages, nonempty text, and no truncation; this may reflect a separate appendix filing rather than an extraction error. Forecast uses the petitioner's account of the jurisdictional and recusal rulings, not independently inspected orders. No target-case outcome was sought or encountered.

The document manifest marks the 142-page petition source truncated; provisioned text ends during the district-court appendix. The main petition and relevant Second Circuit majority/dissent material are available and support the forecast, but later appendices were not assumed available. No BIO was provisioned at this arrival moment; no adverse inference was drawn.

Self-declared hold petition: the SG asks the Court to hold this petition for United States v. Jackson, No. 26-304 (CA9), and dispose of it afterwards. The cell's disposition is therefore a function of the lead docket's grant and merits outcome, and the federal-band arrival anchor (~71% pooled reached rate, sal-v4) mixes lead grants with companion GVRs. I forecast well below the anchor on that basis. Expect this event to stay open until after Jackson is resolved (likely mid-2027).

Decisive forward signals came from public material predating the snapshot, disclosed here for hygiene: (1) the Court denied Atlas Turner v. Welch, No. 25-213 (same receiver, same trial judge) on 2026-01-12 after requesting a response, with Justice Alito recused and no noted dissent; (2) three related petitions are pending on the same territorial question — Nos. 26-159 and 26-263 (from the Third Circuit's Whittaker decision) and the same-day companion No. 26-350 (Altrad), cross-referenced 'Vide' on this docket. The forecast treats the four as a set. This case's own docket (26-328) shows only the filing entry; no disposition exists or was sought.

CourtListener's docket index returned zero results for SCOTUS dockets 25-213, 26-159, 26-263, 26-328 and 26-350, so related-docket state was read from supremecourt.gov docket pages via the engine's web fetch rather than the MCP server. Retrieval ran to about 27 calls, slightly over the advisory 25.
